Chapter 7: Serving Others and Creating Value.
As we grow as leaders, something amazing happens. Our focus starts to shift—from chasing our own achievements, to thinking about how we can really serve the people around us.
Think about it: the true measure of your impact isn’t just what you accomplish, but the positive difference you make in someone else’s life. Service is all about using your strengths, your resources, and your experiences to lift up others.
But you know what? Service doesn’t have to be this huge, dramatic gesture. Sometimes, the smallest acts—like listening with real attention, offering a word of encouragement, or sharing what you’ve learned—can create powerful ripple effects you might never even see.
The secret is simple: approach every interaction with the intention to add value. It doesn’t matter if you’re at work, at home, or out in the community—every moment’s a chance to make a difference.
If you want to bring more service into your day-to-day life, here are a few ideas you can try:
First, just ask, “How can I help?” Look for little ways to support others—sometimes, even a tiny gesture can mean the world.
Next, share what you know—offer your guidance or mentorship without expecting anything in return. That kind of generosity? It’s contagious.
And don’t forget to celebrate the wins of the people around you. When you recognize and uplift someone else’s success, you help them shine even brighter.
Another important part of service is recognizing that everyone has something unique to offer. When you encourage people to lean into their strengths, you multiply your impact. Imagine a teacher who helps a student uncover a hidden talent—not only does that change one life, it can enrich the whole community.
Now, here’s something to pay attention to: Service isn’t about sacrificing yourself or playing the martyr. It’s about finding the sweet spot where what you love intersects with what others need. When your actions reflect both your purpose and your desire to serve, your work feels more meaningful, and your relationships grow deeper.
Over time, adopting this service-first mindset doesn’t just change you—it transforms your team, your organization, even your neighborhood. You end up creating a culture of generosity, trust, and shared success. And those are the real foundations for lasting impact.
